items.funder: Nigerians abroad, through a diaspora bond
items.why: Nigeria sold its first diaspora bond in 2017. A second can finance storage, irrigation and warehouse receipts, so farmers stop selling at harvest-time prices.

items.funder: Pension funds, behind a World Bank guarantee
items.why: Mexico already has a World Bank credit enhancement drawing private capital into its infrastructure. Pointed at municipal water utilities, it lets domestic pension savings buy guaranteed water bonds.

items.funder: The guarantors of debt conversions, and the investors in guaranteed debt
items.why: Barbados has completed two debt conversions. The guarantors who priced them can price a third, with the savings bound to local farms, fisheries and sea farming.

items.funder: Banks, behind a development bank guarantee
items.why: A guaranteed facility brought nine banks to Tanzania’s railway. The same structure can finance last-mile power and electric cookers, recovered through electricity bills.
